newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Violence against women at home on rise in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Violence against women at home on rise in Caribbean.

text.p: Violence at home against women and children is a growing problem in the Caribbean, Trinidad's Prime Minister Basdeo Panday said.

Panday, opening a meeting on Monday of Commonwealth ministers responsible for women's affairs, expressed his concern about "the growing vulnerability of women to violence committed against them and their children".
"Statistical trends indicate the number of women and the incidence of gender-based violence constitute a recurrent problem in the region," he said.

More than 200 delegates from 45 countries are attending the conference on ways to implement a Commonwealth Plan of Action endorsed by last November's summit in New Zealand of the group of former British colonies.
Commonwealth Secretary General Chief Emeka Anyaoku told the meeting there was hardly any area in the Commonwealth where a "gross imbalance" between women and men did not exist.
Anyaoku said the Plan of Action gave women "beacons to guide them out of gender-based violence, poverty, illiteracy, poor health, and the violation of their human rights."
